ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the Lewis structure of hydrogen phosphate, with the central atom being P. The oxygen on the left is labeled Oz, forms a single bond with P, and is drawn with three pairs of lone electron pairs. The oxygen on the right is labeled Oy, forms a double bond with P, and is drawn with two pairs of lone electron pairs. Above and below there is respectively an oxygen labeled Ox; each Ox forms a single bond with P and H respectively, and is drawn with two pairs of lone electron pairs. Reasoning: The formula for the formal charge of oxygen is: formal charge = number of valence electrons 6 - number of nonbonding electrons - 1/2 bonding electrons. Oz has three pairs of lone electron pairs, namely 6 nonbonding electrons, and only one single bond, so formal charge = 6 - 6 - 1 = -1. Oy has two pairs of lone electron pairs, namely 4 nonbonding electrons, and one double bond is equivalent to occupying 2 bonding electrons, so formal charge = 6 - 4 - 2 = 0. Each Ox has two pairs of lone electron pairs, namely 4 nonbonding electrons, and has two single bonds, equivalent to occupying 2 bonding electrons, so formal charge = 6 - 4 - 2 = 0. Therefore the one carrying negative formal charge is Oz.
